note.text: Continental drift proposes that continents have changed position over geological time. Wegener assembled evidence including the broad fit of continental margins, matching fossil distributions and corresponding rocks and ancient climatic indicators. Pangaea names a former supercontinent in this account. The early proposal lacked a convincing mechanism accepted at the time. Later seafloor and plate evidence helped develop plate tectonics. A similar outline alone is suggestive, not the entire argument.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Continental drift proposes that continents have changed position over geological time. Wegener assembled evidence including the broad fit of continental margins, matching fossil distributions and corresponding rocks and ancient climatic indicators. Pangaea names a former supercontinent in this account. The early proposal lacked a convincing mechanism accepted at the time. Later seafloor and plate evidence helped develop plate tectonics. A similar outline alone is suggestive, not the entire argument.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A learner compares continental margins across the Atlantic and then asks whether fossils and rock patterns also correspond. Several independent observations can support a reconstruction better than one jigsaw resemblance. Cameroon is part of the African plate framework, but an exact reconstruction needs geological evidence rather than simply moving modern political borders on paper.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Separate the proposal, the supporting observations and the later mechanism. Use geological rather than national boundaries when considering continental history. Do not describe the early theory's incomplete mechanism as proof that every observation it used was worthless.
